content:
Purpose
- This is a running collation of “hang signatures” we’ve seen with tensor-parallel (TP) under sustained load.
- Audience: runtime oncall, SRE oncall, and anyone doing repro/validation.
- Use this doc to:
  1) match an incident to a signature quickly
  2) decide whether it’s comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler deadlock
  3) pick immediate mitigations (traffic shift, quarantine/reset, config toggles)
  4) link to the right dashboards/traces/log patterns

Notes / hygiene
- Log snippets below are lightly redacted; IDs are representative.
- If you paste new snippets, include:
  - region/pool (hosted vs dedicated), runtime version, model + TP degree
  - what the client saw (timeouts vs stuck streams)
  - whether mitigation worked (shift traffic? restart worker? disable TP?)

Quick taxonomy index (high-level)
- TPH-01: Collective stall / NCCL op never returns (comm stall)
- TPH-02: Async error not surfaced (comm failure masked until later / “silent wedge”)
- TPH-03: Cancel + barrier deadlock (scheduler/group lifecycle)
- TPH-04: Rank skew / partial progress (one rank advances, others flat)
- TPH-05: Scheduler starvation under overload (no deadlock, but “stuck looking”)
- TPH-06: Kernel/stream stall (GPU looks busy, but no forward progress; comm not obviously the culprit)
- TPH-07: Watchdog thrash / repeated quarantines (false positives or borderline slow path)

Primary dashboards / links (internal)
- TP Collectives + Scheduler Health dashboard (spec): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/tp-collectives-scheduler/tp-collectives-and-scheduler-health
- Hosted API error rate (5xx/timeout) by pool/route: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/hosted-errors/hosted-api-errors
- Node GPU telemetry (util/mem/pcie): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/gpu-node/gpu-node-overview
- SRE incident runbook entry (TP hangs): https://confluence.redwoodinference.internal/display/SRE/TP+hang+response

Common fields to search in logs (runtime)
- tp_group_id=<uuid>
- rank=<int>
- model=<name>
- event=tp_collective_* OR event=tp_group_* OR event=scheduler_* OR event=request_cancel*
- request_id=<uuid> (note: not always safe to include in customer-shared logs)

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-01 — Collective stall / NCCL op never returns (COMM STALL)

What it looks like (customer-facing)
- Streaming requests: tokens stop mid-stream; connection stays open until client timeout.
- Non-streaming: request times out (gateway timeout / 504) or returns 5xx after long tail.
- Pool impact: subset of TP groups become “dead capacity”; scheduler continues to send work unless quarantined.

Typical conditions
- High concurrency + mixed sequence lengths; often long-lived streams.
- More common on large Hosted pools and Dedicated clusters with sustained QPS.

Log signature (examples)
[example A — collective started, never completed]
2025-02-13T18:22:41.118Z level=INFO  component=runtime.collectives event=tp_collective_begin op=all_reduce tp_group_id=tpG-7d2c rank=3 stream=cuda:7 seq=step:128 model=rw-llama-70b
2025-02-13T18:22:41.118Z level=INFO  component=runtime.collectives event=tp_collective_begin op=all_reduce tp_group_id=tpG-7d2c rank=4 stream=cuda:7 seq=step:128 model=rw-llama-70b
... (no matching tp_collective_end for > 120s)
2025-02-13T18:24:43.604Z level=WARN component=runtime.watchdog event=tp_forward_progress_stalled tp_group_id=tpG-7d2c stalled_ms=122486 last_progress_step=127 active_requests=6 suspected="collective_stall"

[example B — NCCL debug line in some cases]
2025-02-13T18:22:41.119Z level=DEBUG component=runtime.collectives msg="ncclGroupStart()"
2025-02-13T18:22:41.119Z level=DEBUG component=runtime.collectives msg="ncclAllReduce(count=8388608, dtype=fp16, algo=Ring, proto=Simple)"
... (hang)

Metrics that corroborate
- tp.collective.latency_ms{op_type="all_reduce"} p99 spikes, then flatlines (no observations if we only emit on end)
- tp.rank.progress_step: flat across most ranks
- GPU util may stay high OR drop (depends on where it wedges)

Likely root cause bucket
- NCCL collective stalled due to comm issue or group desync (often paired with TPH-04 rank skew).
- In some cases: async error exists but not surfaced (see TPH-02).

Immediate mitigation (oncall)
- If Hosted: shift traffic away from affected pool/az; drain nodes with repeated tp_group stalls.
- If Dedicated: restart worker process on affected node(s) (fastest customer relief today), or temporarily reduce concurrency.
- If we have watchdog/quarantine enabled: verify group quarantined and removed from scheduling.

Where we’ve seen it
- Sev1 us-east 2025-02-13 (postmortem linked)
- SUP-9841 (customer suspects NCCL stall)

Trace / screenshot stubs
- [TRACE STUB] 2025-02-13 us-east hosted pool: “collective all_reduce step 128 never returns” (attach from profiler once exported)
- [SCREENSHOT STUB] Grafana panel: all_reduce latency p99 spike + watchdog triggers

Fixes in flight
- ENG-2406 / PR-18455: add periodic async error checks + propagate errors
- ENG-2407 / PR-18462: forward-progress watchdog + quarantine

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-02 — Async error not surfaced (SILENT COMM FAILURE / LATE ERROR)

What it looks like
- Similar to TPH-01 but with confusing logs: no explicit NCCL error near the start.
- Sometimes the only error appears much later when the next collective is attempted (or on teardown).

Log signature (examples)
[example A — late surfacing]
2025-02-21T03:11:09.442Z level=INFO  component=runtime.collectives event=tp_collective_begin op=all_gather tp_group_id=tpG-a91f rank=1 model=rw-mixtral
... (stall symptoms)
2025-02-21T03:13:20.007Z level=ERROR component=runtime.collectives event=tp_collective_error tp_group_id=tpG-a91f rank=1 op=all_reduce error="NCCL error: unhandled system error" async="true" hint="error observed on next launch"
2025-02-21T03:13:20.008Z level=WARN component=scheduler event=tp_group_mark_unhealthy tp_group_id=tpG-a91f reason="collective_async_error"

[example B — error only on destroy]
2025-02-21T03:15:44.811Z level=WARN component=runtime.collectives msg="Destroying communicator for tp_group_id=tpG-a91f"
2025-02-21T03:15:44.812Z level=ERROR component=runtime.collectives msg="ncclCommDestroy() failed: unhandled system error"

Metrics
- Sudden spike in request timeouts with minimal correlated “explicit errors” (bad today)
- Later: tp.group.reset_total increments if we tear down

Likely root cause bucket
- Missing/insufficient polling of NCCL async error state.
- CUDA stream/event dependency hides error until we return to CPU control path.

Immediate mitigation
- Same as TPH-01; if you see “error observed on next launch”, treat as comm failure and quarantine/reset group.

Where we’ve seen it
- Staging repro attempts during overload + forced cancel (notes in #eng-runtime)

Trace/screenshot stubs
- [TRACE STUB] “Async error surfaced only on next collective launch” (need Nsight Systems timeline export)

Fixes in flight
- ADR-0147 direction: periodic async error checks + bounded timeouts
- PR-18455: periodic checks (cadence/tuning TBD)

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-03 — Cancel + barrier deadlock (SCHEDULER / GROUP LIFECYCLE)

What it looks like
- Often triggered by streaming disconnects (client closes early) or request-level timeouts.
- Some ranks unwind/cancel; others still waiting in barrier/collective.
- System appears hung but comm path may be fine; it’s a group synchronization logic deadlock.

Repro hint
- Most reliable when:
  - long streaming request A in flight
  - short requests B/C arriving
  - cancel A mid-step while B enters barrier

Log signature (examples)
[example A — cancel arrives mid-step]
2025-02-18T20:05:17.901Z level=INFO component=api.gateway event=request_canceled request_id=req-3f19 reason="client_disconnect" route=/v1/chat/completions
2025-02-18T20:05:17.904Z level=INFO component=scheduler event=cancel_propagated request_id=req-3f19 tp_group_id=tpG-11c8
2025-02-18T20:05:17.905Z level=DEBUG component=scheduler event=tp_barrier_enter tp_group_id=tpG-11c8 barrier="decode_step" request_id=req-8ab2 rank=0
2025-02-18T20:05:17.905Z level=DEBUG component=scheduler event=tp_barrier_enter tp_group_id=tpG-11c8 barrier="decode_step" request_id=req-8ab2 rank=1
... (rank 2/3 never enter; barrier never releases)
2025-02-18T20:06:48.112Z level=WARN component=runtime.watchdog event=tp_forward_progress_stalled tp_group_id=tpG-11c8 stalled_ms=90207 suspected="barrier_deadlock" last_progress_step=44

[example B — scheduler sees queue depth but no dispatch]
2025-02-18T20:06:10.002Z level=INFO component=scheduler event=tp_group_queue_depth tp_group_id=tpG-11c8 queued=17 inflight=0 note="queue growing, dispatch blocked"

Metrics
- scheduler queue depth increases for a tp_group_id
- tp.rank.progress_step flat
- collective latency may NOT spike (because we never reach the collective)

Likely root cause bucket
- Barrier assumes full group participation; cancel path violates invariant.

Immediate mitigation
- Restart worker process hosting the stuck tp_group_id (today’s pragmatic fix).
- In Hosted: drain node if repeated; shift traffic.

Where we’ve seen it
- SUP-9827 mentions “streaming requests hang at high concurrency with TP enabled” + disconnect patterns
- Slack #eng-runtime thread-1739107777 has early repro logs

Trace/screenshot stubs
- [SCREENSHOT STUB] “tp_barrier_enter events for ranks 0/1 only” log view
- [TRACE STUB] Scheduler timeline showing cancel -> barrier -> no progress

Fixes in flight
- ENG-2403 / PR-18441: cancellation-safe barrier semantics + regression test
- ENG-2402 / PR-18432: TP-group state machine to stop scheduling onto quarantined groups

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-04 — Rank skew / partial progress (DESYNC)

What it looks like
- One rank keeps incrementing step counters; others stall.
- Can show up as comm stall (TPH-01) downstream because collectives require all ranks.

Log signature (examples)
[example A — rank skew detector]
2025-02-24T11:44:09.337Z level=WARN component=runtime.sync event=tp_rank_skew_detected tp_group_id=tpG-5a0e max_step=912 min_step=907 skew=5 ranks="0:912,1:912,2:907,3:907" active_requests=4
2025-02-24T11:44:09.338Z level=WARN component=scheduler event=tp_group_mark_unhealthy tp_group_id=tpG-5a0e reason="rank_skew" action="quarantine"

[example B — “rank timed out waiting” (older builds)]
2025-02-10T09:12:55.101Z level=ERROR component=runtime.collectives msg="rank=2 timed out waiting for others at decode_step barrier" tp_group_id=tpG-5a0e

Metrics
- tp.rank.progress_step diverges across ranks (if/when per-rank metrics are available)

Likely root cause bucket
- Cancel/unwind mismatch, or a kernel path diverging by rank (rare but possible)
- Can also be comm-level partial failure (one rank dropped / stream error)

Immediate mitigation
- Quarantine + reset group. If it repeats on same node, drain node.

Where we’ve seen it
- Sporadically in staging stress runs; a few prod incidents mention “one rank pegged” in internal notes.

Fixes in flight
- ENG-2404: per-rank progress counters + structured logs
- ENG-2402/2407: health model + quarantine policy

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-05 — Scheduler starvation under overload (NOT a deadlock)

What it looks like
- Requests time out under heavy load, but system is still making progress; it’s just not fair.
- Often misdiagnosed as “hang” because some requests sit too long.

Log signature (examples)
2025-02-22T16:01:11.003Z level=INFO component=scheduler event=dispatch_loop_lag tp_group_id=tpG-33b2 lag_ms=8421 queued=120 inflight=8 fairness="disabled" note="overload"
2025-02-22T16:01:11.004Z level=INFO component=scheduler event=admission_control throttle="on" reason="queue_depth" pool=hosted-us-east

Metrics
- queue_depth high; but tp.rank.progress_step still increments
- No clear collective stall; GPU util high and changing

Likely root cause bucket
- Backpressure/fairness policy under mixed seq lengths; cancellation storms amplify.

Immediate mitigation
- Reduce max concurrency; enable more aggressive admission control; shift traffic.

Where we’ve seen it
- Hosted peak periods; often clusters with mixed long/short workloads.

Fixes in flight
- ENG-2402/2409 might include tuning; Lena tracking fairness tweaks separately (not all in this project scope).

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-06 — Kernel/stream stall (GPU execution path)

What it looks like
- GPU util sometimes pegged; sometimes weirdly low but process alive.
- Collectives may not be the immediate trigger; it may be a CUDA stream waiting on an event that never completes.

Log signature (examples)
[example A — last log is kernel launch]
2025-02-25T07:45:19.772Z level=INFO component=runtime.kernels event=kernel_launch name="fused_attn_decode" tp_group_id=tpG-8be1 rank=0 stream=cuda:5 seq=step:221
... (no subsequent “kernel_done” / “step_complete” / “collective_begin”)
2025-02-25T07:47:50.008Z level=WARN component=runtime.watchdog event=tp_forward_progress_stalled tp_group_id=tpG-8be1 stalled_ms=150236 suspected="kernel_stall" last_progress_step=220

[example B — cuda error surfaces on next sync]
2025-02-25T07:48:12.901Z level=ERROR component=runtime.cuda msg="CUDA error observed during stream sync" error="an illegal memory access was encountered" tp_group_id=tpG-8be1 rank=0

Metrics
- Per-rank progress flat
- Collective latency not necessarily abnormal (if not reached)

Immediate mitigation
- Restart worker process; drain node if repeated.

Notes
- We need better separation: comm stall vs kernel stall. Today we mostly infer by “was a collective in flight?” which is weak.

Fixes in flight
- ENG-2404/PR-18470: structured stall logs w/ “last known operation” breadcrumbs
- Kernel leads (Hiro/Grace/Yuki) tracking additional microbenchmarks + safe stream/event usage

------------------------------------------------------------
TPH-07 — Watchdog thrash / repeated quarantines (TUNING / FALSE POSITIVES)

What it looks like
- Watchdog triggers frequently during legitimate long steps (e.g., long seq / heavy batch) and quarantines healthy groups.
- Symptoms: increased group resets, elevated tail latency, capacity jitter.

Log signature (examples)
2025-03-01T04:10:33.118Z level=WARN component=runtime.watchdog event=tp_forward_progress_stalled tp_group_id=tpG-1c44 stalled_ms=4021 threshold_ms=4000 sensitivity="high" suspected="unknown" note="no rank skew, no collective in flight"
2025-03-01T04:10:33.119Z level=WARN component=scheduler event=tp_group_quarantined tp_group_id=tpG-1c44 reason="watchdog" action="reset"
2025-03-01T04:10:33.901Z level=INFO component=scheduler event=tp_group_recovered tp_group_id=tpG-1c44 recovery_ms=782
... repeats 12x/hour

Metrics
- tp.watchdog.triggered_total high
- tp.group.reset_total high
- But request errors may not decrease (or may get worse)

Immediate mitigation
- Increase threshold_ms / adjust sensitivity; consider disabling watchdog temporarily in Dedicated if it causes customer impact.

Fixes in flight
- PR-18473 introduces tuning knobs; experiments tracked separately (watchdog thresholds doc)

------------------------------------------------------------
Minimal “signature to action” mapping (oncall cheat sheet)
- If collective_begin exists without collective_end for > threshold AND progress flat: treat as comm stall (TPH-01/02) → quarantine/reset group + consider draining node.
- If cancel_propagated near barrier_enter and then no further progress: likely cancel/barrier deadlock (TPH-03) → restart worker (until fix ships).
- If rank skew detected: quarantine/reset group (TPH-04) and look for correlated cancels.
- If progress increments slowly and queue depth high: overload/starvation (TPH-05) → admission control / traffic shift.
- If last known op is kernel_launch and then nothing: kernel stall (TPH-06) → restart worker; capture GPU trace if reproducible.

What to capture during incident (copy/paste template)
- Region/pool:
- Dedicated customer? (yes/no):
- Runtime version:
- Model + TP degree:
- First symptom time (UTC):
- Example request_id(s) (if safe):
- Affected tp_group_id(s):
- Which signature matches best (TPH-0X):
- Mitigation attempted + outcome:
- Links: Grafana snapshot, log search URL, trace artifact location
